findings.title: Monthly price is recomputed instead of reusing monthlyPriceMinor
findings.explanation: The function reads `PLANS[plan].monthly[currency] * seats` directly and multiplies by 100 later. A `monthlyPriceMinor(plan, currency, seats)` helper already exists just above, and the PR description says the goal is for monthly and annual prices to be computed the same way. Duplicating the lookup means any change to monthly pricing (seat tiers, minimums, per-currency overrides, rounding) will silently not apply to annual pricing. Derive the annual price from `monthlyPriceMinor(...)` so there is a single source of truth.

findings.title: Hardcoded `* 100` is wrong for currencies without 2 decimal places
findings.explanation: Multiplying by 100 assumes every currency has two minor-unit digits. For zero-decimal currencies (JPY, KRW) the result would be 100x too large, and for three-decimal currencies (KWD, BHD) it would be 10x too small. This goes straight into invoices, so it is a billing correctness issue. Take the minor-unit conversion from the same place `monthlyPriceMinor` does, or from a currency exponent table, instead of hardcoding 100.

findings.title: Floating-point arithmetic for money
findings.explanation: `monthly * 12 * 0.9 * 100` chains float multiplications, and 0.9 is not exactly representable. Results that should land on an exact half minor unit can be off by a tiny epsilon, and `Math.round` can then round the wrong way. Use integer math on minor units, for example `Math.round(monthlyMinor * 12 * 9 / 10)`, or `(monthlyMinor * 108) / 10` with an explicit, documented rounding rule. That way checkout and invoices stay deterministic.

findings.title: Magic numbers for months and discount
findings.explanation: `12` and `0.9` are inline literals. Extract named constants such as `ANNUAL_MONTHS` and `ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PERCENT`, or put them in the plan config. The discount will probably be tuned per plan or promotion, and the comment currently has to explain what the code could say itself.

findings.title: No tests and no call sites in the diff
findings.explanation: The description says the checkout page and invoice generator will use this function, but neither is changed here, and no tests are included. Add unit tests covering each plan and currency (including zero-decimal currencies), seat counts of 1 and many, and rounding edge cases. Also confirm that checkout and invoicing actually call this function, so they cannot diverge.

findings.title: Document rounding behavior and return contract
findings.explanation: State in the doc comment that the result is an integer in minor units and how rounding is done (half up via `Math.round`). Also note whether the figure is the total for the year or a monthly-equivalent price, since the name `annualPriceMinor` could be read either way.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Add annual plan pricing

Annual billing launches next month: twelve months for the price of 10.8 (a 10% discount). Adds `annualPriceMinor` next to the monthly price so the checkout page and the invoice generator compute it the same way.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/services/pricing.ts b/src/services/pricing.ts
index 142a18d..f738804 100644
--- a/src/services/pricing.ts
+++ b/src/services/pricing.ts
@@ -16,3 +16,9 @@ export function monthlyPriceMinor(plan: Plan, currency: Currency, seats: number)
 export function planLabel(plan: Plan): string {
   return plan === 'team' ? 'Team' : 'Business'
 }
+
+// Annual billing: twelve months with a 10% discount, in minor units for the invoice.
+export function annualPriceMinor(plan: Plan, currency: Currency, seats: number): number {
+  const monthly = PLANS[plan].monthly[currency] * seats
+  return Math.round(monthly * 12 * 0.9 * 100)
+}
```
